text: Meridian Steel Fabricators, ticket forty-six-forty-one. A plant controller bought a new stamping press in August. It's September now, still no depreciation expense for it. Did the process not run?

First question, before touching this one asset: did depreciation run at all for the book and period? If the whole book showed nothing this period, that's a much bigger ticket. Here, the run completed successfully, and every other asset in the book shows September depreciation just fine. This is isolated to one asset.

Checking that one asset: the stamping press isn't showing as a depreciating asset at all — it never made it out of Mass Additions into the active register. Checking the Mass Additions queue confirms it: the invoice line is sitting there with status ON HOLD, not Posted. It's missing a required asset category, something Prepare Mass Additions couldn't default on its own.

So the asset simply doesn't exist yet in the register — and something that doesn't exist in the register can't depreciate. The fix: assign the correct asset category, set the queue status to Post, run Post Mass Additions, and confirm it enters the register with its real August in-service date, not September. That matters because depreciation needs to catch up for the month it missed, not just start going forward from today.

Resolution note: confirm this was isolated to one asset, name the exact hold reason, and verify both August and September depreciation now show correctly. Full detail on Mass Additions queue mechanics is next — lesson twenty-two: mass additions that aren't posting.
